title: Summary and Note-making — condensing any passage
notes: **Summary:** read for gist → underline key ideas → draft (author's main idea first, then 2–4 key supports) → cut modifiers/examples to fit the word limit → verify meaning is unchanged and nothing is copied.

**Summary grammar:** four paraphrase moves — synonym swap (threat→danger), word-class change (pollute→pollution), voice change (active↔passive), sentence merge; report verbs frame it ('the passage argues…'). Never add your own opinion.

**Note-making:** TITLE in caps → numbered sub-headings (1, 2, 3 — noun phrases, one per paragraph) → compact key-phrase points (a, b, c) → abbreviations (&, →, e.g.) with an 'Abbreviations used' note.
**Note grammar:** nominalise verbs for headings ('agricultural expansion'); drop articles/auxiliaries in points; every point under 7 words.
**Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).
examShortTricks: Trick 1: Note-making format: title → indented points → sub-points (a, b) → abbreviations with a key; the visual format itself carries marks.
Trick 2: Keep only ONE idea per point; drop examples, repetitions and statistics — selection is the tested skill.
Trick 3: Summary vs notes: summary is connected prose in your own words; notes are fragments — do not mix the two forms.
practiceQuestions: Q. Make notes on a passage with a title and three main points. (3 marks) — heading, indented points with sub-points, key to abbreviations.
Q. What should be excluded from a summary? (1 mark) — examples, repetition and minor details.
